Code in simple
English.

Simple is a programming language made of short English sentences. Learn how coding really works in Simple, then step up to real Python and Java, all in your browser.

Try it right now
Press Run, then change a word and run it again.
What is it?

A language in sentences

Every line reads like English and ends with a period. No curly brackets, no semicolons, no type words. Simple works out the details, then shows you the same program in Python, Java, C++, C, assembly and bytes.

Who invented it?

Bharat Seethagari

Started on October 25, 2026 with one big question: could coding be simple enough for anyone to start? One day later, Simple had its own lessons, practice and IDE.

“Every expert was once a beginner. Write your first line today.”

When?

October 25, 2026

Simple grew in one day from a single question into a language with its own IDE, lessons, practice problems and this demo website.

Why?

Coding should be readable

  • Real languages are full of symbols that scare beginners.
  • Simple lets anyone code from the first minute.
  • Every rule matches an idea in Python and Java, so nothing is wasted.
  • The AI coach gives hints instead of answers, so you still learn.

Everything in Simple demo

One place to go from your first line of code to real Python and Java.

150 lessons13 units, from "Say hello" to apps with buttons, then Python, Java and how computers run code.
1,020 problems34 topics in Simple, Python and Java. Each has 10 easy, 10 medium and 10 hard problems, checked automatically.
Three languagesWrite and run Simple, Python and Java right in the page. No installing anything.
Your own accountYour progress is saved, so you can carry on where you stopped. Earn points and badges, and spend them on themes and profile icons.

How Simple works

When you press Run, your sentences travel down through the same layers every real language uses.

1. You write SimpleShort English sentences with simple rules.
2. Simple checks itIt finds mistakes and explains them in plain words. It also works out every kind of value.
3. It translatesThe same program appears in Python, Java, C++ and C.
4. It breaks it into stepsEach line becomes tiny machine steps called assembly.
5. It runs the bytesThose steps become numbers (bytes) that a small machine in the page runs.

Less code, same app

Line counts of the example apps (not counting blank lines), measured from the real translations Simple writes.

The question that started it

“Why do computers need such complicated languages? Could there be a language so simple that anyone could start coding right away, and that still teaches what coding really is?”

Bharat Seethagari, October 25, 2026

Learn to code, step by step

Each lesson explains one idea, shows an example you can run, and gives you a small task. Lessons start in Simple and end in real Python and Java.
